title: A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale

segments.ch03.s0300: They stood dripping on the bank, a queer-looking party.
segments.ch03.s0310: The first question was how to get dry again.
segments.ch03.s0320: What I was going to say was this.
segments.ch03.s0330: The best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race.
segments.ch03.s0350: Why, the best way to explain it is to do it.
segments.ch03.s0360: First it marked out a race-course, in a sort of circle.
segments.ch03.s0370: The exact shape does not matter.
segments.ch03.s0380: Then all the party were placed along the course, here and there.
segments.ch03.s0390: There was no one, two, three, and away.
segments.ch03.s0400: They began running when they liked, and left off when they liked.
segments.ch03.s0410: So it was not easy to know when the race was over.
segments.ch03.s0420: After half an hour or so, they were quite dry again.
segments.ch03.s0440: They all crowded round it, panting, and asking who had won.
segments.ch03.s0450: The Dodo sat for a long time with one finger pressed upon its forehead.
segments.ch03.s0460: Everybody has won, and all must have prizes.
segments.ch03.s0470: Then a chorus of voices asked who was to give the prizes.
segments.ch03.s0490: The whole party crowded round Alice, calling out for prizes.
segments.ch03.s0500: She pulled a box of comfits out of her pocket and handed them round.
segments.ch03.s0510: There was exactly one each, all round.
segments.ch03.s0520: But she must have a prize herself, you know.
segments.ch03.s0530: What else have you got in your pocket?
segments.ch03.s0560: We beg your acceptance of this elegant thimble.
segments.ch03.s0570: Alice bowed, and took the thimble, looking as solemn as she could.
